{{short description|American mathematician}}

'''Sommer Elizabeth Gentry''' is an American mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[United States Naval Academy]] and as a research associate in surgery at the [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]]. Her research concerns [[operations research]] and its applications to the optimization of [[organ transplant]]s,{{r|usna}} and has led to the discovery of geographic inequities in organ allocation.{{r|lung}} She is also interested in dancing, teaches [[Swing (dance)|swing dancing]] at the Naval Academy,{{r|swing}} and wrote her doctoral dissertation on the mathematics and robotics of dance.{{r|mgp}}

==Early life and education==
Gentry is originally from California.{{r|pair}} As a girl, she was inspired to continue in mathematics by the [[recreational mathematics]] columns of [[Martin Gardner]] and [[Ivars Peterson]].{{r|angle}} In 1993, as a senior at [[Thousand Oaks High School]], Gentry had the highest individual score at the [[Ventura County, California]] county-level [[United States Academic Decathlon|Academic Decathlon]].{{r|acadeca}}
She graduated from [[Stanford University]] in 1998, with both a bachelor's degree in mathematical and computational sciences and a master's degree in engineering-economic systems and operations research.

She completed her Ph.D. in electrical engineering and computer science at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2005.{{r|usna}} Her dissertation, ''Dancing cheek to cheek: haptic communication between partner dancers and swing as a finite state machine'', was supervised by Eric Feron.{{r|mgp}} In her doctoral research, she modeled the language and notation of dance mathematically using [[finite-state machine]]s, programmed a robot to dance,{{r|dwr}} and used her model to improve [[Haptic technology|haptic]] communications between humans and robots, with the goal of eventually producing human-machine surgical collaborations that could be more effective than human or robotic surgeons working alone.{{r|balance|jive}}

==Other activities==
Gentry is married to Israeli surgeon [[Dorry Segev]]. She met him at a [[Lindy Hop]] dance competition in 1999, and a few years later they won the British Championship in Lindy Hop. She has also worked with Segev on the [[Kidney Paired Donation]] program.{{r|pair}}

In 2017, Gentry was a competitor on the [[List of programs broadcast by Fox|Fox Television]] game show ''Superhuman''.{{r|superhuman}}

She has also been a vocal critic of the airport passenger screening procedures of the US [[Transportation Security Administration]], which she characterizes as [[sexual assault]].{{r|tsa}}

==Recognition==
Gentry won the [[Henry L. Alder Award]] for Distinguished Teaching by a Beginning Faculty Member of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2009.{{r|alder}} She won the [[Navy Meritorious Civilian Service Award]] in 2014,{{r|usna}} and in the same year was a finalist for the [[INFORMS]] Daniel H. Wagner Prize for Excellence in Operations Research Practice.{{r|wagner}} She will deliver a [[Mathematical Association of America|Mathematical Association of America (MAA)]] invited lecture at [[MathFest]] 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Invited Addresses {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/node/2567109/|access-date=2021-06-04|website=www.maa.org}}</ref>
